name: First sparks
subtitle: Something between us
hints: Share a song or a post first, then let the question come up naturally.
Offer your own answer first: ‘I will go first… now your turn.’ It feels more like sharing than an interview.
Make it a little game: ‘Shall we play a question game? Honest answers only!’
A quiet moment before bed is a lovely time to say, ‘Something just crossed my mind…’
topics: What was your very first impression of me?
How would you describe our relationship right now?
If we spent all of tomorrow together, where would you take me?
Have you secretly browsed my social media? How far back did you go?
Has your heart ever raced while we were chatting?
Do you deliberately wait before replying to someone you like?
What is one thing about me that you find especially attractive?
For a movie together, would you pick a horror film or a romance? Why?
What does your ideal date look like?
Is there a song that makes you think of me?
Do you think people of different genders can be just friends?
If you did not hear from me all day, would you reach out first?
How do you know you are falling for someone? What gives you away?
Have you ever saved a screenshot of one of our conversations?
If you gave me a nickname that only you used, what would it be?
Do you prefer making the first move or being pursued?
Do you check your phone first thing on a weekend morning? Whose message are you hoping for?
Have you ever dressed up especially to see someone?
If we played truth or dare, what question would you dread most?
What is the sweetest part of the almost-dating stage?
If we had only one umbrella in the rain, how would we share it?
Would you mind someone you like looking through your phone?
What have I done so far that left the strongest impression on you?
If I said I was missing you a little today, how would you reply?
What is one quality you cannot compromise on in a partner?
Which makes your heart flutter more: holding hands or a hug?
Is there something you have wanted to tell me but have not said?
If our relationship were a kind of weather, what would it be?
Could you fall for someone because of their voice?
What would you like us to do the next time we meet?
If you wrote the opening line of our story right now, what would it be?

name: Choosing us
subtitle: From a crush to a couple
hints: Begin with a memory: ‘I was looking at our old messages…’ Then ease into the question.
Frame it as curiosity: ‘There is something I have always wondered about you.’
Ask while walking side by side on a date. It can feel easier than sitting face to face.
Start with a sincere compliment. Feeling appreciated makes it easier to open up.
topics: Do you remember the moment we became a couple? What were you thinking?
Before we got together, how long did you wonder whether to make a move?
When did you realize you really liked me?
Were you nervous on our first date? Did you prepare anything beforehand?
How did you describe me to your best friend?
Once we got together, how was I different from what you had imagined?
How did you really feel the first time we held hands?
What was the first photo of me you saved on your phone?
What has changed most in your life since we started dating?
What little tradition would you like for our anniversary?
Which three words would you use to describe us right now?
Would you like to introduce me to your family and friends? How would you introduce me?
Who said they liked the other person first? Was it hard to say?
What worried you most at the beginning of our relationship?
Which of us likes to stay close more?
Was there a moment when you thought, ‘This is my person’?
What do you most like me to call you?
What little detail do you love about the way we chat?
How does being with me compare with the relationship you once imagined?
What were you wearing when we first met? Do you remember what I wore?
Have you ever proudly shown a friend our messages?
What little habit have you changed or picked up because of me?
If we could start again, would you begin our relationship the same way?
In what way are we most alike?
On days we cannot meet, what do you most wish we could do together?
What small keepsake connected to me have you held on to?
Do love songs feel different now? Which song has changed for you?
How often would you like us to say ‘I like you’?
On a scale of one to ten, how would you rate our relationship right now, and why?

name: Everyday love
subtitle: Romance in the little things
hints: Ask while cooking, walking or relaxing on the sofa. Everyday questions fit everyday moments.
Use what is happening around you: ‘Speaking of that, I just wanted to ask…’
Start with two options, then ask why they chose one.
After their answer, a gentle ‘Why is that?’ means more than a string of new questions.
topics: What little habit do you love most about our everyday life?
Am I the first person you think of when you wake up? Be honest.
If we made breakfast together, what would each of us do?
What daily habit would you most like us to build together?
Which meal I cooked or takeaway I ordered do you remember best?
Do you prefer my relaxed at-home look or when I dress up?
What would you sneak into our shopping cart at the supermarket?
Which of us is grumpier after waking up?
What do you like us to talk about before bed?
If our daily life were a documentary, what would you call it?
Do you prefer holding hands with fingers intertwined or a gentle clasp?
After a busy day, what would you most like to hear me say?
Which of us remembers the little things better? Give an example.
Would you like to swap schedules for a day and experience each other's life?
Which household chore would you happily take on, and which would you avoid?
Which photo of us on your phone is your favorite?
If we had one regular ‘us day’ each week, how would you spend it?
What little thing I do without thinking do you find cutest?
Would you rather stay home together or go out together?
We always struggle to choose takeaway. What permanent rule would you make?
When you are ill, what do you most want me to do for you?
What is our most comfortable way to cuddle?
Do you squeeze toothpaste from the middle or the end? Can we agree on this?
If we got a pet, what would you choose and what would you name it?
What scent do you most like on me?
What would you most like us to do on a rainy weekend afternoon?
What small ritual is missing from our everyday life?
Which of us has better taste in clothes? Which of my outfits would you change?
If we watched a series together, could you resist watching ahead?
Which of my everyday skills would you like to learn?
If a dish described our daily life, what dish would it be?

name: Little adventures
subtitle: Try something new together
hints: Ask an imaginative question with a perfectly serious face. The contrast makes it fun.
Share your own ridiculous answer first and invite them to add to it.
Make a playful bet: ‘If our answers match, you buy the bubble tea tonight.’
Waiting for a bus, queuing or sitting in traffic is perfect for a little imagination.
topics: If we won ten million, what would we do first?
If you could teleport once, where would you take me?
If we swapped bodies for 24 hours, what would you most want to do?
If you had to eat one food for a year, what would you choose? Could you live with my choice?
What is number one on your bucket list for us?
If we ran a market stall together, what would suit us best to sell?
If you signed me up for a hobby class, which would you pick?
When we travel, are you a planner or a go-with-the-flow person?
If you could meet a younger version of me, what would you say?
If we played a game as a team, which of us would get frustrated first?
If our story became a film, who would you want to play you?
At an amusement park together, which ride would you try first?
Would you try bungee jumping or skydiving with me? Pick one.
If we opened a little shop, what would we sell and what would we call it?
What secret code would you invent just for us?
Would you try a whole day with no phones, just the two of us?
If you could have one superpower for our relationship, what would it be?
Let's invent a silly competition. What would give you the best chance of winning?
If we were stranded on an island, which of us would struggle more?
What sport would you most like to try with me?
If we wrote a book together, what would it be about?
If you impersonated me, which phrase of mine would you use first?
Would you take a spontaneous trip with me? Pick a direction right now.
If our relationship were a game, what would it take to complete it?
Whose childhood photos are funnier? Dare to swap them now?
If we could be animals for a day, what animal would you want me to be?
What little joy do you keep to yourself? Would you share it with me once?
Would you rather watch a sunrise or a sunset together? Why?
Which TV show for pairs would we be best suited to join?
Plan a little adventure for us next month. What is the theme?

name: Memory lane
subtitle: The lives that led us here
hints: Look through old photos together. Memories tend to bring their own questions.
Tell a small childhood story first and let them share one too.
Play a few old songs on a quiet evening before talking about the past.
Ask about the details of a memory: ‘How did that feel at the time?’
topics: What is one of your happiest childhood memories?
What was your childhood nickname, and who gave it to you?
What were you like at school? Very different from now?
When did you have your first crush?
What job did you dream of as a child? How do you feel about it now?
Do you have a favorite old family photo? Tell me its story.
Who are you most grateful to for helping you grow up?
What is the most rebellious thing you have ever done?
Is there an old song that takes you straight back to a certain moment?
When did you first leave home? Do you remember how that day felt?
Which year of your life do you miss most, and why?
Are you still afraid of something that scared you as a child?
Where did you have the most delicious bite of food you can remember?
What was your first phone like? What did you do with it first?
Tell me an embarrassing childhood story you have never told anyone.
How did you meet your best friend?
Which goodbye hurt most while you were growing up?
What is something you have stuck with for the longest time?
If you could relive one day from your past, which would you choose?
What do you miss most about your hometown?
What was your family's most special holiday tradition when you were little?
What first made you feel that you had grown up?
Who was your biggest idol once? Do you still like them?
Is there an old possession you cannot bear to throw away?
What was the person who sat next to you at school like?
What is the bravest decision you have made?
Before meeting me, when did you change most as a person?
Do you remember the first holiday we celebrated together?
Which moment between us do you treasure most so far?
If we made a museum of our memories, what would be the first exhibit?
Would you ten years ago have imagined life looking like this?

name: Opening up
subtitle: A little closer to your heart
hints: Choose an unhurried moment when you both feel relaxed. Deeper questions deserve time.
Share a feeling before asking: ‘I have felt closer to you lately, and I wondered…’
If you both enjoy it, hold hands or cuddle while talking. Feeling safe helps honesty.
If they pause, give them time. The words that follow may matter most.
topics: When do you feel safest with me?
When did thinking of me last make you smile to yourself?
When you feel low, would you like my company or some space?
Do you feel understood by me? What little moment shows it?
What does being loved actually feel like to you?
How would you most like me to express love: words, actions or gifts?
Was there a moment when you suddenly felt you could not do without me?
Are you afraid to be vulnerable with me? Why?
What is something I said that has stayed with you?
How do you think we have built trust, little by little?
What do you really feel inside when I compliment you?
Would you share how you truly feel today?
Have you ever worried about me? What happened?
Can you tell when I am upset even if I say I am fine?
What side of you do you most want me to understand?
In love, do you need more to feel needed or to feel cared for?
Is there a hurt you would like me to handle gently?
When did you feel our relationship grow a little closer?
How soon would you like us to make up after an argument? Who reaches out first?
What does home feel like to you? Have I ever given you that feeling?
Where were you the last time you missed me?
If our love had a temperature, what would it be right now?
Does loving someone deeply make you stronger or more vulnerable?
What small thing I do makes you feel truly loved?
Would you feel comfortable crying in front of me?
Do you feel comfortable when we sit together in silence?
Have you ever secretly made a wish for our relationship?
What would you most like me to whisper in your ear?
What personal growth in this relationship makes you proud?
Does ‘I love you’ feel more accurate than ‘I like you’ now?

name: Close to you
subtitle: The sweetness of being near
hints: Try a gentle whisper, if you are both comfortable. A softer voice can change the mood.
Ask with a smile so it feels like flirting, rather than a test.
A cozy moment before sleep can make affectionate questions feel natural.
Respond to their answer with affection they enjoy, such as their favorite kind of hug.
topics: What is your favorite way for us to hug?
Which reassures you most: holding hands, hugging or kissing?
How do you like me to look at you?
What goes through your mind when you rest on my shoulder?
What little affectionate ritual would you like before leaving and after coming home?
How would you rate our first kiss?
Would you rather I stroked your hair or held your hand?
Shall we slow dance together? To which song?
Which everyday moment feels more romantic than a special occasion?
What view would you most like us to enjoy while cuddling?
Would you rather receive a handwritten love letter or a late-night voice message?
Dare to tell me where you are most ticklish?
When did we share a look that said everything?
How much togetherness feels right for you?
If the power went out tonight and we had only candles and each other, what would you do?
Do you prefer a good-morning kiss or a good-night kiss?
Would you choose a hot spring together or a night under the stars?
Shall we invent a little affectionate gesture that only we understand?
Which feels more intimate: a quiet embrace or an animated conversation?
How close do you like us to be when we whisper?
In a crowd, how would you like me to show that we are together?
Would you like a hug from behind while doing the dishes?
When your hands are cold in winter, would you slip them into my pocket?
What is your most romantic confession scene? Shall we make it happen?
What do you most like to see me wearing?
Close your eyes and picture my face. What do you notice first?
If you planned an anniversary kiss, where would it happen?
Would you like our photos to look sweet, cool or silly?
How would you make our good-night ritual even sweeter?
Would you let me give you a proper neck and shoulder massage?
If I were beside you right now, what would you most want me to do?

name: Understanding us
subtitle: Finding our way through differences
hints: Save these questions for a calm moment when you both feel good, away from an argument.
Start with ‘I sometimes worry…’ rather than ‘You always…’ to make space for listening.
Offer reassurance: ‘I really want to understand how you feel. Take your time.’
Walking side by side can make a sensitive conversation feel less intense.
topics: What do you think was behind our most recent disagreement?
When you are angry, what would you like me to do first?
Which little habit of mine bothers you most? You can be honest today.
Have you ever said something you did not mean during an argument?
What could we improve about the way we communicate?
Which hurts a relationship more: arguing or the silent treatment?
When we disagree, how would you like us to make the final decision?
What emotional boundary matters to you? Have I crossed it without realizing?
How can I support you when you need time alone?
Is there a misunderstanding you still want to clear up?
Which matters more to you: an apology or a change in behavior?
Is there a habit of mine you have put up with without mentioning it?
If your close friend and I fell out, how would you handle it?
What ground rule would you like us to have for arguments?
Do you sound sharper when you are tired? How can I recognize it?
Which time making up helped us understand each other better?
Would you mind me dining alone with a friend of another gender? Where is your boundary?
How do you feel when I reject an idea of yours?
What is the difference between being accepting and suppressing your own needs?
Which of us is more stubborn? Give an example.
How would you like me to raise something that is bothering me about your behavior?
Is there a topic you have been avoiding discussing with me?
Where is the limit to changing yourself for a partner?
If we had not really talked for several days, would you break the silence?
What tone of voice do you most dread hearing from me?
What have you been compromising on for me for a long time?
How would you rate our ability to handle conflict? How could we improve?
When you express a need, would you prefer an immediate yes or a discussion first?
Can you accept that occasional disagreements are part of a relationship?
What is one small thing you would like me to start changing today?
If you summed up our learning to get along in one sentence, what would you say?

name: What matters
subtitle: Honest talks about real life
hints: Begin with something you read: ‘I saw a discussion about this today. What do you think?’
Make room for honesty: ‘There is no right answer. I want to understand your view.’
If you disagree, ask why before responding. Understanding comes before persuasion.
One thoughtful conversation is enough. You do not need to tackle every practical question at once.
topics: How should we balance money and our relationship?
If we managed money together, how would you divide it?
How important is it for partners to come from similar backgrounds?
How do you prioritize work and life?
How long could you manage a long-distance relationship? Where is your limit?
Do you think love has to lead to marriage?
What does caring for and respecting your parents mean to you?
What would you do if our parents disapproved of our relationship?
How should we divide responsibilities at home?
Do partners need to keep each other updated about where they are?
Do you lean toward saving for later or enjoying life now?
What is an absolute deal-breaker in a relationship for you?
If a friend asked to borrow a large sum, would you discuss it with me first?
What are your honest thoughts on having children someday?
What is our biggest difference in attitudes toward spending?
How would you weigh a career opportunity against our relationship?
Would you prefer an ambitious big-city life or a quieter life in a small town?
How do you define betrayal? Does an emotional affair count?
What privacy boundaries should partners have?
Would a large difference in our incomes affect how you feel?
How do you feel about traditional marriage gifts such as bride price and dowry?
How much do differences in education and life experience matter between partners?
Would you move to an unfamiliar city for your partner?
What are the three most important things in a relationship? Rank them.
How do you feel about each of us keeping a few small secrets?
If you won a huge prize, would you quit your job? Would you want me to?
How much has your family background shaped your ideas about love?
Whose family should we visit for holidays? Do you have a plan?
Can practical pressures defeat love? How could we prevent that?
Can different core values be reconciled, or is compatibility essential from the start?

name: Our tomorrow
subtitle: Dreaming a life together
hints: Let the scene spark the question: a lovely house or someone else's wedding can be a natural opening.
Invite a picture: ‘Close your eyes and imagine a weekend morning five years from now…’
Write down each other's answers and revisit them in six months.
Ask ‘And then?’ to help their picture of the future become more vivid.
topics: Have you imagined our life five years from now? Describe it.
In which city would you like us to make our future home?
What would our ideal home look like? What would grow on the balcony?
What family tradition would you like us to create?
What kind of life would you like us to have after retirement?
Which three places must we visit together?
What rhythm would you like our future weekends to have?
If we had a spare room for anything we wanted, what would you make it?
What would be the first line of a letter to us five years from now?
What goal would you most like us to achieve together in the next year?
What do you think we will be like as an elderly couple?
Where would you like to go for our first anniversary trip?
What personal space should each of us keep in the future?
If we have children, what is one thing you most want to teach them?
What kind of marriage proposal would you like?
Who will be the head chef in our future kitchen, and what is their signature dish?
What ideas do you have for our future savings plan?
What do you hope we will be doing on this day ten years from now?
What would you like to be the centerpiece of our future living room?
If we started a business together, what would it be?
How many pets will we have, and what will their names be?
By what age would you like to reach your most important life milestones?
Would you like a lively wedding or a celebration just for the two of us?
What kind of person do you hope I will be in ten years?
If you drew our future home, which corner would you draw first?
What one thing could we promise to do together every year?
How would you like us to face major difficulties together?
If we have a child, who do you think they would resemble? Who would you hope for?
What would you name our first car together?
Is there a promise you feel we simply must fulfill?
What would you put in a time capsule for us to open in ten years?

name: Choosing forever
subtitle: Promises we mean to keep
hints: Choose a meaningful moment: an anniversary, a trip or a carefully prepared dinner.
Offer your own commitment first. A promise is something to share freely.
Give each other your full attention. These questions deserve to be heard.
If they need time, say ‘There is no rush.’ Giving space can be a promise too.
topics: What does a promise mean to you?
What makes you sure you want to keep walking through life with me?
Do you think our relationship can stand the test of time?
Is marriage an endpoint or a new beginning to you?
Would you keep holding my hand through our hardest times?
If I became seriously ill, how would you care for me?
Where does our relationship sit among your life priorities?
What would you like to say first when you meet my parents?
Which promise between us have you quietly kept in mind?
Is loyalty an instinct or a choice?
When the initial passion fades, what keeps love going?
Would you openly commit to one thing you will keep doing for me?
If one of us dies first in old age, how would you hope the other lives?
What is the hardest part of growing old together?
Could we agree not to threaten a breakup in anger?
What boundary would you commit to respecting in this relationship?
When do you think it is right to meet each other's parents?
Would you tell our story to our future children? Where would you begin?
If you could choose again, would you choose me? How long did you think about that?
Which of us do you think will say ‘Let's get married’ first?
What are your thoughts about rings? Which hand would you wear one on?
Let's write ten rules for our home. What is the first?
When did you start thinking in terms of ‘we’ rather than ‘I’?
Does marriage frighten you? What worries you most, and how could we face it together?
Would you revisit this conversation with me on this day every year?
If one vow captured how you feel about me, what would it be?
What is the smallest daily act that helps love last a lifetime?
Would you put my name on every page of your plans for the rest of your life?
What between us do you most want to honor?
Would you make a ten-year promise with me? What would we promise?

name: Soul to soul
subtitle: Finding our answer in each other
hints: Choose a peaceful moment, late at night or early in the morning, with room to listen.
Begin with gratitude: ‘Thank you for being here with me.’ Let the question follow.
If words are hard to say, write them down and exchange notes.
After their answer, offer a long hug if they would like one. Some answers need only warmth.
topics: Do you think we are soulmates? Why?
What did I do this year that moved you most?
What is the most important thing you have learned from me?
If we had only one day left to live, how would you spend it with me?
What do you think is the deepest form of love?
What do we understand about each other without words? Give an example.
What burden of mine would you most like to help carry?
Since meeting me, what part of yourself have you made peace with?
What is the biggest difference in our love compared with a year ago?
If there were another life, how would you like to meet me in it?
Is there a thank-you you have always wanted to say to me? Say it now.
Which of my strengths do you think the world underestimates most?
If our souls were two things that went together, what would they be?
Would you still love me when I am hardest to love? What might that look like?
Was there a moment when it felt as if we had known each other all our lives?
What do you hope our love will eventually become?
Which moment from this past year together would you frame and keep?
Which is rarer: being understood or being loved?
If you wrote one line of poetry about us, what would it be?
What missing part of yourself have you found in me?
What would you most like to protect in me: my innocence, my dreams or something else?
When no one else understands you, do you trust that I will be on your side?
Do you think we met by chance or by fate?
Close your eyes and name three reasons you love me. Do not overthink it.
What would you like people to say when they describe our relationship?
If our story had an inscription, where would you put it and what would it say?
Is a deep connection something you find or something you build? Which is ours?
Of these 366 days of questions, which question has stayed with you most?
What would you say to us a year ago, just starting this journey?
If the length of a hug expressed your love right now, how long would you hold me?
As a new year opens a new chapter for us, what first sentence would you write?
